title: Two Phaedras

panels.visual: King Theseus of Athens (older now, short grey-streaked beard, crown, cloak) with his arm round his grown-up son Hippolytus (young, athletic hunter with a bow and two hounds) in front of the palace; an inset portrait of a fierce Amazon queen with a shield
panels.caption: Years after the Minotaur, Theseus was king of Athens. His grown-up son Hippolytus was the son of an Amazon queen.

panels.visual: The wedding of Theseus and Phaedra (young Cretan woman, long dark wavy hair, thin gold crown, red Minoan dress); Hippolytus standing politely to one side
panels.caption: Theseus married again: Phaedra, Ariadne's little sister. So Phaedra became Hippolytus's stepmother.

panels.visual: Hippolytus hunting deer in a moonlit forest with his hounds, and beside him the goddess Artemis (young huntress, short tunic, silver bow, crescent moon on her brow) smiling approvingly
panels.caption: Hippolytus loved hunting. He worshipped Artemis, goddess of the hunt, who wanted nothing to do with love.

panels.visual: Hippolytus walking straight past a rose-covered statue of Aphrodite without a glance; the real goddess Aphrodite (golden hair, pink gown, doves) appearing behind the statue, red-faced with jealousy, fists clenched
panels.caption: He ignored Aphrodite, goddess of love. The two goddesses were rivals, and Aphrodite was furious.

panels.visual: Aphrodite on a cloud shooting a glowing pink arrow into Phaedra's heart while Phaedra, in the palace, stares at Hippolytus passing in the courtyard
panels.caption: To punish him, Aphrodite made Phaedra fall madly in love with her own stepson.

panels.visual: Phaedra's old nurse whispering the secret to Hippolytus; Hippolytus recoiling in disgust, hand raised
panels.caption: When Hippolytus found out, he was disgusted and refused.

speech.speaker: Hippolytus
speech.text: Never! She is my father's wife!

panels.visual: Phaedra alone at night writing a letter by the light of an oil lamp, crying, ashamed and terrified
panels.caption: Phaedra was ashamed and terrified of what he might tell. She wrote a letter with a lie about him in it.

panels.visual: Theseus coming home to the palace to find servants weeping, an overturned stool and a fallen red veil on the floor, the letter in his shaking hands; no body shown
panels.caption: Then she hanged herself. Theseus came home and found the letter.

panels.visual: Theseus raging on the seashore with the letter, shouting at the stormy sea, the giant face of the sea god Poseidon rising in the waves
panels.caption: Theseus believed the lie. Poseidon had once promised him one wish.

panels.visual: Hippolytus driving a two-horse chariot along a rocky shore as a monstrous bull bursts out of a giant wave; the horses rear and bolt; then the chariot smashing on the rocks, red splashes, Hippolytus tangled in the reins
panels.caption: A monstrous bull burst out of the waves. The horses bolted and dragged Hippolytus over the rocks.

panels.visual: Theseus kneeling and holding his broken, dying son; the goddess Artemis glowing silver above them, pointing at the torn letter
panels.caption: Artemis appeared and told Theseus the truth. Father and son forgave each other. Then Hippolytus died.

panels.visual: The Theatre of Dionysus in Athens in 428 BC: a packed audience on the stone seats watching masked actors on stage; inset, an old poster from Paris 1677 reading 'Phèdre'
panels.caption: Euripides' play Hippolytus was first performed in this theatre in 428 BC and won first prize. In Paris, Racine retold it as Phèdre.

mood: Tragic mood for this story: warm daylight turning to stormy grey and night, dark-red ink as the single accent colour; the crash shown with blood as splashes and drips, never wounds; suitable for children aged 9 to 11.
